extracted.intended_audience: general educated British public, clergy, educators, and policymakers (late 18th-century)
extracted.subtask_description: A polemical essay warning about the dangers of secret/mystic societies and 'Illuminatism', arguing for vigilance in education, public morals, and the preservation of religion, patriotism, and open institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women must assert dignity to command respect
rubrics_metrics.description: As long as the women ask nothing of the men but fondness and admiration, they will get nothing else--they will never be respected. But let them rouse themselves, assert their dignity, by shewing their own elevated sentiments of human nature, and by asking up to this claim, and they may then command the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages women to assert elevated sentiments and dignity rather than seek only fondness and admiration; presenting this as a means to secure respect and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy in associations implies danger or frivolity
rubrics_metrics.description: If there be a necessity for secrecy, the purpose of the association is either frivolous, or it is selfish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy is suspect: the author argues that anything of true importance will not need to be kept secret and that hugging a secret of 'mighty importance' contradicts professed brotherly love. Secret ends tend toward selfish or frivolous aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret and mystical societies progress from frivolity to sedition
rubrics_metrics.description: Their uniform progress has been from frivolity and nonsense to wickedness and sedition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical pattern offered as an evaluative principle: lodges and mysteries begin with trivial occupations and, as they cease to satisfy members, are repurposed to concealed and dangerous activities leading to public mischief and subversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open communication is essential for the discovery of truth
rubrics_metrics.description: All who have seriously employed themselves in the discovery of truth have found the great advantages of open communication of sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that true inquiry requires calm and openness, and that a hankering after secrets is inimical to sober search for truth; secrecy should be distrusted as obscuring and corrupting inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charitable acts need not be secret
rubrics_metrics.description: The distribution of charity needs be no secret, and it is but a very small part of the employment of the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private charity should be achievable within ordinary acquaintance circles; secretive charitable schemes are unnecessary and secrecy around charity is a red flag for misuse of meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mysterious associations with secret objects become public nuisances
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole history of man is a proof of this position. In no age or country has there ever appeared a mysterious association which did not in time become a public nuisance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites ancient mysteries (Eleusinian, Pythagorean) as having external signs shocking to decency and civil order; secrecy enables leaders to shift aims and to exercise unchecked power over followers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declamations of universal philanthropy are dangerous
rubrics_metrics.description: All declamations on universal philanthropy are dangerous. Their natural and immediate effect on the mind is to increase the discontents of the unfortunate, and of those in the laborious ranks of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that exhortations to cosmopolitan or universal philanthropy undermine attachments to family, patriotism, and social duties, fomenting discontent among the lower ranks without practical improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain patriotism and natural attachments (family preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The preference which natural instinct gives parents for their children... surely no one can doubt of the propriety of maintaining this in its full force, subject however to the precise laws of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defends patriotism and familial affections as socially necessary instincts that should be preserved (while constrained by justice) against cosmopolitan doctrines that would dissolve them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vigilance over instructors of youth; examine their principles
rubrics_metrics.description: We should be particularly careful to prevent them, and ought to examine with anxious attention the manner of thinking of all who offer themselves for teachers of youth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers and educational officers should be persons of decent manners and approved principles; the author warns of deliberate attempts to gain influence over students and to inculcate subversive ideas, recommending scrutiny of character and principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be especially observant of 'men of talents' in influential offices
rubrics_metrics.description: We should be particularly observant of the character and principles of Men of Talents, who offer themselves for these offices, because their influence must be very great.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Talented individuals may exert disproportionate influence and thus warrant greater scrutiny for loyalty to social and moral norms; talent combined with heterodox principles is presented as particularly dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distrust those very cautious in declaring opinions on core questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Such should always be filled by men of immaculate characters and approved principles; and, in times like the present, where the most essential questions are the subjects of frequent discussion, we should always consider with some distrust the men who are very cautious in declaring their opinions on these questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Silence or excessive caution about fundamental political/religious questions is portrayed as suspicious and a potential sign of hidden, dangerous views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourage secret assemblies, perfectionist political talk, and immorality
rubrics_metrics.description: We should discourage all secret assemblies, which afford opportunities to the disaffected, and all conversations which foster any notions of political perfection... Above all, we should be careful to discourage and check immorality and licentiousness in every shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy recommendations: actively oppose secret meetings, utopian/perfectionist rhetoric, and public immorality as measures to protect government and social order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public instructors must actively defend Religion and Virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: If there has ever been a season in which it was proper to call upon the public instructors of the nation to exert themselves in the cause of Religion and Virtue, it is surely the present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that religion and virtue are principal bulwarks against conspiratorial subversion and that educators' failure to act will be interpreted as defeat; they should proactively inculcate these principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderate criticism of government with sympathy, not perpetual condemnation
rubrics_metrics.description: Real love for our country and its government would (I think) induce a person to mix with his criticisms some sentiments of sympathy with the embarrassment of a minister... The critic would recollect that the minister was a man, subject to error, but not necessarily nor altogether base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and political critics should temper fault-finding with understanding of the burdens of governance; habitually portraying government as always at fault encourages discontent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware philosophies that explain moral sentiments mechanistically
rubrics_metrics.description: Any very perfect theory of moral sentiments must have something of this tendency... increase of virtuous affections in general has not been the fruit of modern Illumination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against reducing affections and religion to mechanical descriptions (vibrations/æther), as such accounts tend to flatten moral feelings and abet atheism/materialism that undermine social bonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: National establishments of religion help preserve religion and social order
rubrics_metrics.description: I cannot help thinking that, in the present condition of Europe, religion would desert the world, if the opinions of men were not directed, in some proper degree, by National Establishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defends state-supported religion as a means of directing public opinion and maintaining religious sentiment; rejects the view that establishments are the sole source of corruption but affirms their present utility.
